1.explanation:
1. Wrap your container in Carbon’s <Theme> component with theme="g10" or theme="g100" to simulate a high-contrast/light-inverse or dark-inverse context.
2. Reference the new CSS custom properties (set by the SASS tokens) in your styled component:
   • --cds-inverse-01 for the background
   • --cds-text-inverse for the default text/link color
   • --cds-link-hover-inverse for the hover state
   • --cds-link-inverse-active for the active state
3. Observe that on hover and active the link should now switch to Blue 30/Gray 10 in g10, and Blue 70/Gray 100 in g100. If the new tokens are missing or not applied, you will see the wrong colors (the issue you are reproducing).
1.bug_scenario: The bug occurs inside high-contrast “inverse” containers (for example, inside a Tooltip or Popover rendered with the g10/g100 Theme). Inline links that use the `$link-inverse` token should have distinct hover and active colors, but because the new tokens (`$link-inverse-hover` and `$link-inverse-active`) were not wired up, the hover and active states fall back to the default link tokens. In a g10 (light inverse) container the hover state should be Blue 30 (#a6c8ff) and the active state Gray 10 (#f4f4f4); in g100 (dark inverse) the hover state should be Blue 70 (#0043ce) and the active state Gray 100 (#161616). Instead you see the normal link hover (Blue 60) and active (Blue 80) colors.
